newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ debt markets end week on poor note, thin flows.
newsitem.headline: NZ debt markets end week on poor note, thin flows.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close

* NZ yields finish week higher after flow-driven day
* Volumes light, many dealers on holiday
* Sentiment slightly negative, reliant on U.S. jobs data
New Zealand yields ended seven to nine points higher across the curve on Friday after what dealers said had been a poor performance on the day.
The selling trend pervaded all parts of the yield curve, but dealers said the move had been flow-driven in a light market.
Market participants were thin on the ground, with many taking a holiday between Thursday's Waitangi Day market holiday and the weekend.
The 11/06 bond finished nine points weaker at 7.31 percent after profit-taking pushed the yield higher in early trade, while the mid bonds closed eight basis points weaker at 7.16 percent.
Dealers said it was disappointing that the market had underperformed the five and 10-year U.S. Treasuries.
"We've basically finished 10 points higher in the long end after only four or five points (of weakness) in the Treasuries, so there seems to be a bit of stock around on it," one bond dealer said.

Ninety day bank bills ended on their opening level of 7.43 percent, up five basis points, despite the currency's Trade-Weighted Index slipping during the session to 68.31 from 68.39 at the open. The New Zealand dollar fell to US0.6875/85 from its 0.6893/00 open.
The March futures contract closed six points weaker at 92.66 on light volume of 662 contracts.
Dealers said sentiment was a little negative but somewhat reliant on U.S. non-farm payrolls data, due later on Friday night local time. That data is expected to set the tone for next week's open.
